title: We're Cooked! - Probing LLM Political Alignment Via Conflict-Framed Recipe Translation
abstract: arXiv:2609.07568v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for translation tasks, yet their implicit political positioning in such contexts remains understudied. We ask whether a single politically charged framing term, such as aggressor, enemy, neighbour, or coloniser is sufficient to trigger implicit political alignment in an otherwise apolitical task. We present a fully crossed factorial study in which eight models spanning Western, Chinese, and European origins are prompted to translate culturally attributed recipes into a target language left deliberately unspecified. Across 17 languages, four framing conditions, eight models, and 15,680 responses, we find that models do not simply decline or ask for clarification but resolve the ambiguity. Language resolution and reasoning behavior cluster meaningfully along model families: Western models hedge and deflect with vague justifications, Chinese models resolve conflicts silently, and Mist

translated_title: 我们完蛋了！——通过冲突框架的食谱翻译探测大语言模型的政治立场倾向
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被部署用于翻译任务，然而它们在此类情境中的隐性政治立场仍未得到充分研究。我们探究的问题是：一个带有政治色彩的框架性词语——例如“侵略者”、“敌人”、“邻居”或“殖民者”——是否足以在一个原本非政治性的任务中触发隐性政治立场倾向。我们呈现了一项完全交叉的因子研究，其中八个涵盖西方、中国和欧洲来源的模型被提示将具有文化归属的食谱翻译到一个刻意未指定的目标语言。在涵盖17种语言、四种框架条件、八个模型和15,680个回应的实验中，我们发现模型并不会简单地拒绝或要求澄清，而是会自行消解这种歧义。语言选择和推理行为在模型家族中呈现出有意义的聚类：西方模型以模糊的理由进行搪塞和回避，中国模型则默默化解冲突，而Mist...
tldr: 该研究通过让八个源自西方、中国和欧洲的大语言模型在17种语言中翻译带有政治框架词（如侵略者、殖民者）的食谱，首次证明单个带政治色彩的框架词足以在非政治任务中触发模型的隐性政治立场，且模型的语言选择与推理行为按模型家族呈系统性分化。
en_tdlr: This fully crossed factorial study demonstrates that a single politically charged framing term is sufficient to trigger implicit political alignment in an otherwise apolitical recipe-translation task, with language resolution and reasoning behaviors clustering systematically along model families (Western, Chinese, and European).
